headline: pki.cmp.build now assembles the nested PKIMessage body an RA uses to forward or batch complete messages.
summary: A `nested` PKIBody carries a sequence of complete PKIMessages, each keeping its own protection, so a registration authority can forward or batch messages that other parties signed without re-signing their contents (RFC 9810 sec. 5.1.3.4). `pki.cmp.build` gains a `nested` body arm that takes an array of PKIMessage DER. Each entry is parsed and validated as a PKIMessage before it is wrapped; an empty array, or an entry that is not a valid PKIMessage, is refused with `cmp/bad-input`. The parser already surfaces a received `nested` body as its raw arm, so the producing and parsing sides round-trip. The wrapped messages are surfaced as raw bytes and are never verified on the caller's behalf, because each one carries its own protection that the recipient checks.

Added: `pki.cmp.build` accepts a `nested` body: `{ body: { nested: [pkiMessageDer, ...] } }` wraps an array of complete PKIMessage DER as a `NestedMessageContent` under the explicit `[20]` PKIBody tag (RFC 9810 sec. 5.1.3.4). This is the body a registration authority sends when it forwards or batches messages that were protected by other parties. Each entry is parsed as a PKIMessage before it is included, so a malformed entry is caught when the message is built. An empty array is refused, because the field is `SIZE (1..MAX)`. Both failures raise `cmp/bad-input`. Each wrapped message keeps its own protection, which the recipient validates; `pki.cmp.build` does not re-sign or verify the contents.
